firstMismatch.javascript: UnsupportedHeroCommandBoundaryError: encumberMessage is not available for otyp 321
firstMismatch.c: invent.c:hold_another_object() returns the reacquired lit oil potion after calling encumber_msg()

summary: The admitted v76 action lights one potion from an inventory stack of three. apply.c:light_cocktail() splits the selected oil potion, starts its burn, removes the child from inventory, and calls invent.c:hold_another_object() to reacquire it. The C helper adds it, updates inventory, then calls pickup.c:encumber_msg(). JavaScript ports these helpers, but light_cocktail() supplies only the message hook, so invent.js:hold_another_object() fails closed at step 125 when it requires the missing encumberMessage callback. The later snuff and merge actions occur after this first cause.

source.branch: In light_cocktail(), the item is unlit, the hero is not swallowed or underwater, and quan > 1. The selected potion is split, made known, lit with begin_burn(), detached from inventory, and passed to invent.c:hold_another_object(). On successful reacquisition, hold_another_object() updates inventory and calls pickup.c:encumber_msg() before returning the object pointer.
callers: apply.c:doapply() POT_OIL arm calls light_cocktail(&obj); js/apply.js:doapply() awaits light_cocktail(objp, state, env) and then reads objp.obj.
dependencies: invent.c:hold_another_object() is implemented by js/invent.js and requires an injected encumberMessage hook after update_inventory().
pickup.c:encumber_msg() is implemented by js/pickup.js and updates go.oldcap after any load-change message.

evidence: The hosted v76 evaluation records 125/225 screens and cursors matched and 2370/2378 RNG entries matched; JavaScript stops at zero-based step 125 on the missing encumberMessage hook.

At the failing action, the hero applies one item from a three-potion oil stack. C reaches apply.c:light_cocktail() with the unlit potion, splits one child, calls makeknown() and begin_burn(), removes the split child, and calls invent.c:hold_another_object().

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:1704-1765 orders the split, burn, and reacquisition. invent.c:1208-1293 adds a holdable item, calls update_inventory(), then calls encumber_msg() at line 1290. pickup.c:1977-2020 implements that message and updates go.oldcap.

The saved accepted-prefix trace matches all 125 preceding screens, RNG entries, and cursors, then reports: encumberMessage is not available for otyp 321. js/apply.js:light_cocktail() builds hooks with message only; js/invent.js:hold_another_object() requires the acquisition encumberMessage callback after adding the item.

The source correction belongs at the light_cocktail() caller: pass the existing pickup.c:encumber_msg port through the hold_another_object hook, preserving a supplied caller hook when present. The existing invent.c and pickup.c implementations need no edits.
selectionReason: Selected synthetic/v76/v76-oil-snuff-merge-action2 from its hosted v76 evaluation. The first mismatch is the split-one reacquisition inside apply.c:light_cocktail(): JS has added the child but refuses before the existing C encumber_msg call because its caller omitted the required hook. The later snuff/merge actions are downstream and are not the first cause.

resolution.sourceChange: js/apply.js:light_cocktail now supplies the existing pickup.c:encumber_msg port as the encumberMessage hook when reacquiring the split oil potion; an explicit caller hook remains authoritative, and the same message sink is used for the burden update.
resolution.runtimeEvidence: The production #apply path lights one item from a three-potion stack, reacquires the burning child, refreshes burden state, then continues through subsequent snuff/merge actions. The complete 225-step admitted segment matches screens, RNG, and cursors.
